summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Wrinkle Mini Class - Currently Updated to P5 p01 ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will explore how to create and manipulate wrinkles in fabrics using Marvelous Designer. We will cover factors that affect wrinkles and how to optimize grid settings for better simulation effects. ## Creating the Board Now we have a board. First, copy a similar board and sew it together. To see the wrinkle effect more clearly, I lengthen the board below. ## Understanding Wrinkles in Fabric When the two long lines are sewn together, there is no wrinkle when it naturally falls, unless there is an external force dragging or supporting a certain point. However, when the length of the two lines is the same, the longer side board will pile up along the sewing line, making the wrinkles more obvious. ## Activating the Center Point The position along the sewing line is the most obvious. The center point of the double-sided selection can be activated. After that, it can be retracted or rotated with the center as the basis. Once retracted, the length of the sewing line changes. ## Simulation of the Fabric After opening the simulation, the board above is frozen, so it will not be deformed. The longer board will form wrinkles due to the function of the sewing line. The characteristic of this wrinkle is that there are many wrinkles along the sewing line. ## Particle Strength and Texture The particle strength will also affect the texture and effect of the wrinkle. The board is made up of a triangular grid. The particle strength is the distance between the top of the grid; the smaller the particle strength, the more the grid surface. After reducing the particle strength, the number of faces increases, leading to smoother curves and more detailed wrinkles. ## Changing Grid Types In addition to particle strength, the simulation effect will also be affected by the type of grid. In the menu in the right-hand corner, you can select to convert the grid to a rectangular grid. The fabric of the rectangular grid will be more flexible than the triangular grid and will have fewer uneven parts. The rectangular grid is prioritized in the outer or inner line of the board. ## Organizing the Grid Layout It is possible to arrange the grid from the outside line or the inside line and then move to the middle position. However, the layout may become messy, causing the fold of the panel to be less smooth. The panel can also be divided into four parts and remeshed. After remeshing, the grid layout is organized according to the layout of the 2D window, resulting in a very neat grid arrangement. ## Resetting the Grid After each change of the particle diameter, the reset grid will rearrange itself. If the panel is rotated or has a special shape, the grid arrangement may become crooked, which can hinder simulation performance. If you just rotate without changing the particle diameter, there should be no issue. ## Particle Diameter Adjustments For rectangular panels, simply rotating them to the level or value position and then changing the particle diameter will return it to the original state. After the simulation, even though the particle diameter is set to 20, the neat grid arrangement results in smooth fold areas. The overall shape and number of folds remain consistent with the previous design. ## Grid Type Calculations However, the reset grid version differs from the default grid type, leading to larger calculations. When the particle diameter is relatively small (like 5 or below), there may be some lags. The triangular shape also has its own length, which remains stable. Sometimes, reducing the particle diameter for the entire panel is unnecessary, as long as the details are shown. ## Dividing the Grid To divide the grid, select the grid brush tool to choose certain panels and divide the grid. After dividing, the particle diameter of the grid becomes smaller, and the number of grid surfaces increases. You may notice some inconspicuous cracks appear. Once the division command is applied, if the overall particle diameter is reduced, the area of division will also reduce. ## Visualizing Divisions Generally speaking, when a part is divided, it will display in a special color. If you can't see it from a certain perspective, you can zoom in or out to visualize it better. To delete the division, right-click to return to the normal grid layout. ## Adjusting Panel Gaps For long and short gaps, we can directly increase the width and length of the panel to create more space. The same adjustment can be applied to the vertical grid. The middle line of the grid is the horizontal line of the grid, while the vertical line is the horizontal line of the grid. ## Conclusion We can also make the grid larger to enhance the overall design. Thank you for watching this tutorial. You have made significant progress in understanding the basics of fabric in Marvelous Designer. ```
